slides.purpose: Understand the deck explains a proposed personal-account journey

audience_state.after: Understand the deck explains a proposed personal-account journey

visible_copy.title: One account across providers
body: A proposed way to move between providers

visual_plan.subject: one person's account across two illustrative providers
relationships: the same account links to both providers
visual_plan.approximate_composition: a short left-to-right journey in the existing clean reference style

speaker_notes.text:
Hi everyone.

Let me show you the access journey we are proposing. Imagine a colleague who needs to open two different providers. This is a simple illustration.

The idea is that the colleague uses their own account for both. Let us follow that journey one step at a time.

slides.purpose: Understand where sign-in sits in the journey

audience_state.before: Know this is one person's account
audience_state.after: Understand where sign-in sits in the journey

visible_copy.title: Start with your account
body: Sign in before opening a provider

visual_plan.subject: a person signs in using their personal account
relationships: person uses the account before entering the provider path
visual_plan.approximate_composition: large account symbol on left; sign-in doorway in middle; first provider at right

speaker_notes.text:
First, our colleague starts with their own account.

Signing in lets the service recognise who is arriving. In this proposed journey, that is the account the colleague will use as they move between providers.

Now they can choose the first provider.

slides.purpose: Understand that provider permission is a separate check

audience_state.before: Know the account recognises a person
audience_state.after: Understand that provider permission is a separate check

visual_plan.subject: recognised person opens a provider and access is checked
visual_plan.approximate_composition: first provider highlighted; second provider quieter in background; simple gate at entry

speaker_notes.text:
Now the colleague chooses the provider they need.

The proposal keeps a separate access check there. Having an account answers who the person is; the provider still needs to decide whether the person may use it.

That matters when the colleague moves to another provider.
speaker_notes.transition: Switch providers without implying automatic permission

slides.purpose: Understand account reuse without assuming automatic access or proven session reuse

audience_state.before: Know access is checked at a provider
audience_state.after: Understand account reuse without assuming automatic access or proven session reuse

visual_plan.subject: the same account reaches a second provider with its own permission check
visual_plan.approximate_composition: journey advances right; account appearance stays constant; second provider highlighted

speaker_notes.text:
So, the colleague moves to the second provider using the same account.

That does not mean the two providers give the colleague the same access. Each provider can have its own permissions.

We also have not settled every sign-in detail. Using the same account alone does not tell us whether another sign-in step will appear. What stays clear is the personal account and the separate provider access.
speaker_notes.transition: Recap what the access journey changes

slides.purpose: Be able to explain the proposed journey and identify support questions without a technical decision request

audience_state.after: Be able to explain the proposed journey and identify support questions without a technical decision request

visual_plan.subject: account continuity and distinct provider access
relationships: account is reused across both provider paths
support handling remains an open question
visual_plan.approximate_composition: compact journey across top; account and access concepts beneath; open support question at right

speaker_notes.text:
That is the access journey in the proposal: the person carries one account across providers, and provider access remains a separate question.

For operations, the support path will matter too. We still need to work out how account questions and provider access questions reach the right help.

Is the journey clear, and where would someone need more guidance?
